lessons.title: સવાર (savār) — hear morning first
lessons.gloss: morning, heard before it is shown as a reading target

segments.text: Listen twice: savār. It means morning. Hold the sound and the meaning together; the Gujarati spelling waits for a later lesson in this chapter.

segments.instruction: "savār" when you picture early light, and nothing when you picture a dark sky
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "savār" when you picture early light, and nothing when you picture a dark sky]

segments.text: What part of the day is savār? (Morning.)
Source: Cambridge: morning.

segments.prompt: What does savār mean?

feedback.incorrect: Listen once more: savār — morning.

lessons.title: બપોર (bapor) — hear midday first
lessons.gloss: midday, afternoon, heard against the morning word

segments.text: Say savār from morning. Now listen twice: bapor. It means midday, the middle hours that English also calls the afternoon.

segments.instruction: "savār" or "bapor" as you hear the English cue morning or midday
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "savār" or "bapor" as you hear the English cue morning or midday]

segments.text: Which of the two comes first in a day? (Savār — morning.)
Source: Cambridge: afternoon.

segments.prompt: Give the English meanings of savār and bapor, in that order.

feedback.correct: Two times of day now stand apart by sound.
feedback.incorrect: Hear the pair once more: savār — morning; bapor — midday.

lessons.title: સાંજ (sānj) — hear evening first
lessons.gloss: evening, heard third in the day sequence

segments.text: Say savār, then bapor. Now listen twice: sānj. It means evening. The nasal in the middle is light — the tongue never quite closes.

segments.instruction: the three words in day order — savār, bapor, sānj
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the three words in day order — *savār*, *bapor*, *sānj*]

segments.text: What does sānj mean? (Evening.)
Source: Cambridge: evening.

segments.prompt: Say the three words for morning, midday, and evening in day order.

feedback.correct: Three times of day, in order, by ear.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the missed word, then say all three again.

lessons.title: રાત (rāt) — hear night first
lessons.gloss: night, the fourth and last part of the day cycle

segments.text: Say bapor, then sānj. Now listen twice: rāt. It means night. Three sounds, one beat.

segments.instruction: whichever of bapor, sānj, rāt answers the English cue you hear
segments.source: [YOU SAY: whichever of *bapor*, *sānj*, *rāt* answers the English cue you hear]

segments.text: What does rāt mean? (Night.)
Source: Cambridge: night.

segments.prompt: Which is evening and which is night: sānj, rāt?

feedback.incorrect: Hear the two once more: sānj — evening; rāt — night.

lessons.title: The day in four parts, by ear
lessons.gloss: four parts of the day, retrieved by ear alone

segments.text: Nothing new arrives here. Say the first part of the day, then the last, before any list is read to you.
Keep two scores. Listening goes from sound to meaning; speaking goes from meaning to sound. A strong score in one cannot cover a miss in the other.

segments.prompt: Hear this shuffled row and give the four English meanings: rāt — savār — sānj — bapor.

feedback.incorrect: Replay only the missed sound, then answer that one again.

segments.prompt: Say the four Gujarati words in day order, from the English cues alone.

feedback.incorrect: Repair only the missed cue, then say the four in order again.

segments.text: Which two of the four have you not yet seen written? (All four — the writing of rāt begins in the next lesson, with signs you already know.)
Sources: Cambridge: morning, afternoon, evening, and night.

lessons.title: Rāt reaches the page
lessons.gloss: night, now written with three signs already taught

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Before anything is uncovered, say the Gujarati word for night.

Uncover રાત (rāt) once. Nothing in it is new: ર was taught in the courtesy chapter, the ા stroke in the very first one, and ત beside it. Name the three parts aloud in order, then read the whole word once.

segments.prompt: Read this word aloud and give its meaning: રાત (rāt).

feedback.correct: You read rāt from signs you already knew.
feedback.incorrect: Name the three signs one at a time, then read the word again.

blocks.title: Writing — guided copy, model in view

segments.text: Keep the model in view and copy રાત (rāt) once, left to right. Repair one shape if it needs it; do not start a row.

segments.prompt: With the model in view, copy night once.

feedback.incorrect: Copy the three parts in order, checking each against the model.

segments.text: How many signs make rāt, and were any of them new today? (Three, and none was new.)
Source: Cambridge: night.

lessons.title: દિવસ (divas) — hear day first
lessons.gloss: day, the whole span the four parts divide

segments.text: Say the word for night, and recall the three signs that wrote it. Now listen twice: divas. It means day — the whole span that savār, bapor, sānj, and rāt divide between them.

segments.instruction: "divas" for the whole span, then "savār" for its first part
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "divas" for the whole span, then "savār" for its first part]

segments.text: Is divas a part of the day or the whole of it? (The whole of it.)
Source: Cambridge: day.

segments.prompt: What does divas mean?

feedback.incorrect: Listen once more: divas — day.

lessons.title: મહિનો (mahino) — hear month
lessons.gloss: month, the span above the day

segments.text: Say the word for day, and say how many signs wrote rāt. Now listen twice: mahino. It means month — the span that holds many a divas.

segments.instruction: "divas" for the smaller span, then "mahino" for the larger one
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "divas" for the smaller span, then "mahino" for the larger one]

segments.text: What does mahino mean? (Month.)
Source: Cambridge: month.

segments.prompt: Which is the larger span, divas or mahino, and what does each mean?
acceptedResponses: mahino is larger; divas — day, mahino — month

feedback.correct: Day and month stay apart by size.
feedback.incorrect: Hear them once more: divas — day; mahino — month.

lessons.title: આજ (āj) — hear today first
lessons.gloss: today, the day you are standing in

segments.text: Say the word for day, then the word for month. Now listen twice: āj. It means today — this divas, the one you are standing in. Two sounds only.

segments.instruction: "divas" for any day, then "āj" for this one
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "divas" for any day, then "āj" for this one]

segments.text: What does āj mean? (Today.)
Source: Cambridge: today.

segments.prompt: Which means day in general, and which means today: divas, āj?

feedback.correct: The general span and this one stay apart.
feedback.incorrect: Hear them once more: divas — day; āj — today.

lessons.title: Āj reaches the page
lessons.gloss: today, now written with two signs already taught

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Before anything is uncovered, say today, then day, in Gujarati.
Uncover આજ (āj) once. Two signs, both old friends: the standalone આ that opens āvjo, and the જ of the doorway nine. Name them in order, then read the word once.

segments.prompt: Read this word aloud and give its meaning: આજ (āj).

feedback.correct: You read āj from signs you already knew.
feedback.incorrect: Name the two signs one at a time, then read the word again.

blocks.title: Writing — guided copy, model in view

segments.text: Keep the model in view and copy આજ (āj) once. Repair one shape if it needs it; do not start a row.

segments.prompt: With the model in view, copy today once.

feedback.incorrect: Copy the two parts in order, checking each against the model.

segments.text: Which two signs write āj, and where had you met each before? (આ from āvjo, and જ from the doorway nine.)
Source: Cambridge: today.
Say today, name the two signs that write it, then say month. Now listen twice: atyāre. It means now.
Three widths of time, narrowing:
mahino — many days together.
āj — this one whole day.
atyāre — this moment inside it.

segments.instruction: the three in narrowing order — mahino, āj, atyāre
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the three in narrowing order — *mahino*, *āj*, *atyāre*]

segments.text: What does atyāre mean? (Now.)
Source: Cambridge: now.

segments.prompt: Which is the narrower span, āj or atyāre, and what does the narrower one mean?

feedback.correct: Atyāre is the moment inside the day.
feedback.incorrect: Hear the two once more: āj — today; atyāre — now.

lessons.title: Payoff — eight time words in four skills
lessons.headword: સવાર — બપોર — સાંજ — રાત — દિવસ — મહિનો — આજ — અત્યારે
lessons.romanization: savār — bapor — sānj — rāt — divas — mahino — āj — atyāre
lessons.gloss: eight time words in four separately scored skills

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say the first part of a day, then the word for this moment. Keep four scores below. A strong score in one skill cannot cover a miss in another.
Listening — meaning from sound. Eight items, shuffled, once through.
Speaking — sound from meaning. Six items from English cues, no Gujarati model in view.
Reading — a cold pair. Only the two words this chapter put on the page are read; the other six stay oral until a later chapter writes them.

segments.prompt: Hear this shuffled row and give the eight English meanings: atyāre — sānj — divas — mahino — savār — rāt — āj — bapor.
acceptedResponses: now — evening — day — month — morning — night — today — midday
now evening day month morning night today midday
now evening day month morning night today afternoon

feedback.incorrect: Replay only a missed sound, then answer that one again.

segments.prompt: From English cues alone, say the four parts of a day in order, then today and now.
acceptedResponses: savār — bapor — sānj — rāt — āj — atyāre
savar bapor sanj rat aaj atyaare

feedback.incorrect: Repair only a missed cue, then say that one again.

segments.prompt: Read this shuffled pair and give each meaning: આજ (āj) — રાત (rāt).

feedback.incorrect: Name the signs of the missed word, then read that card again.

blocks.title: Writing — from meaning, with every model covered

segments.text: Study the two written words for five seconds, cover every model, and write them from meaning. Record writing on its own, then repair only a missed word.

segments.prompt: Study both words for five seconds, cover every model, then write night and today in that order.

feedback.correct: Both words came back after the model was hidden.
feedback.incorrect: Uncover only the missed word, study it again, and rewrite that one.

segments.text: How many of the eight can you say, and how many can you write? (Eight by ear, two by hand — and the six waiting are a later chapter's work.)
Sources: Cambridge: morning, day, today, and now.

lessons.title: The eight time words return at R1
lessons.headword: સવાર — બપોર — સાંજ — રાત — દિવસ — મહિનો — આજ — અત્યારે
lessons.romanization: savār — bapor — sānj — rāt — divas — mahino — āj — atyāre
lessons.gloss: retrieve the eight time words at their first spacing window

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Nothing new arrives here. Say the word for now before any list is read to you, then recall which four scores the payoff kept apart.
Keep the same four scores the payoff kept. Listening runs sound to meaning; speaking runs meaning to sound.

segments.prompt: Hear this shuffled row and give the eight English meanings: mahino — rāt — āj — bapor — atyāre — savār — divas — sānj.
acceptedResponses: month — night — today — midday — now — morning — day — evening
month night today midday now morning day evening
month night today afternoon now morning day evening

feedback.incorrect: Replay only a missed sound, then answer that one again.

segments.prompt: From English cues alone, say day, month, today, and now in Gujarati.

feedback.incorrect: Repair only a missed cue, then say that one again.

blocks.title: Writing — from meaning, with every model covered

segments.text: Cover every Gujarati model and write the two words from sound alone. Record writing on its own; a strong listening score cannot cover a miss here.

segments.prompt: Cover every model. Write today, then night, from the spoken words alone.

feedback.correct: Both words came back from sound with no model in view.
feedback.incorrect: Check only the missed word, cover it again, and rewrite that one.

segments.text: How far after the payoff did this return come? (One lesson — the first spacing window.)
Sources: Cambridge: month and now.

lessons.title: The map words return at a third window
lessons.gloss: the newest map words return at a genuine third spacing window

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The five newest place words have not been asked for since the chapter that taught them. Before any list is read, say village and shop in Gujarati.
Listening — meaning from sound. Five items, shuffled, once through.
Speaking — sound from meaning. Three items from English cues alone.
Keep the scores apart, exactly as the payoffs that first taught these words did.

segments.prompt: Hear this shuffled row and give the five English meanings: dukān — rasto — gām — shahar — shāḷā.

feedback.correct: Listening is 5/5 at a real distance.
feedback.incorrect: Replay only a missed sound, then answer that one again.

segments.prompt: Say city, school, and road in Gujarati, in that order, with no model in view.

feedback.incorrect: Repair only a missed word, then say that cue again.

blocks.title: Writing — from meaning, with every model covered

segments.text: Cover every Gujarati model and write the two words from meaning. Record writing on its own, then repair only a missed word.

segments.prompt: Cover every model. Write village, then shop, from meaning alone.

feedback.correct: Both spellings came back with no model in view.
feedback.incorrect: Check only the missed word, cover it again, and rewrite that one.

segments.text: Why does this return come here rather than beside the words that taught it? (Because retrieval at a distance is what makes the words durable, and a return next door would have measured nothing.)
Sources: Cambridge: city, school, road, and village.
